name: Withagen recurrent prolapse trial
aliases: Prolift versus conventional repair in recurrent prolapse
question: Does trocar-guided polypropylene mesh reduce treated-compartment anatomic failure compared with conventional vaginal repair for recurrent prolapse?

design.population: Women undergoing surgery for recurrent stage II or higher anterior or posterior pelvic organ prolapse at 13 Dutch centers.
design.locator: Withagen 2011, Materials and Methods; Milani 2018 PDF pp847,849, Figure 1

verdictNote: Treated-compartment anatomy improved, while patient-reported improvement was similar and mesh exposure occurred.
takeaway: Trocar-guided Prolift polypropylene mesh reduced 12-month treated-compartment anatomic failure versus conventional vaginal native-tissue repair for recurrent prolapse, without greater patient-reported improvement; mesh exposure occurred in 14/83 examined women (16.9%).

delivery.label: Operative technique
delivery.value: Prolift trocar-guided anterior, posterior or total tension-free mesh; full-thickness midline fibromuscular incision and vaginal closure without tissue resection. Conventional repair allowed compartment-specific plication and surgeon-selected apical procedures.
delivery.locator: Withagen 2011, Materials and Methods, surgical procedures

delivery.label: Concomitant procedures
delivery.value: No hysterectomy or T incision with mesh; sacrospinous fixation or modified Manchester-Fothergill allowed. Conventional surgery was surgeon selected without adjunct mesh.
delivery.locator: Withagen 2011, Materials and Methods, surgical procedures

delivery.label: Surgeon training
delivery.value: 22 experienced pelvic-floor gynecologists were trained by an authorized Prolift instructor; individual trial volumes ranged from one to 72 repairs.
